Whatever may be thought of Midhat’s reforms by others,  we were enabled fully to appreciate one of them—the tramroad  running from El Mina to Tripoli. As we waited, seated on a  pile of sacks outside a maize store, the scene around us was  painful to a degree; for on every side lay the poor camels,  shortly to be laden, groaning pitiably, their owners busy  dressing the sores made by the unwieldy saddles, and stuffing  cotton-wool into the bruised parts. I was thankful indeed  when the tramcar at last appeared. It is drawn by mules, and  does the distance between the two towns in twenty minutes.   I mounted with Andrew to the top of it, and
